objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have had further practice identifying subjects, verbs, and objects and will be better able to write complete, correctly punctuated sentences.
materials: - Coursebook: First Steps in Academic Writing, pp 13-17

stages.stage_aim: To activate learners’ recall of the sentence definition from Part 1 and introduce the concepts of subject, verb, and object
stages.procedure:
- Quick quiz: "What three things must a complete sentence have?" Elicit answers. "What was the one exception?" (command sentences). 2 min.
- Display a model sentence on screen: "My roommate lost his keys." Ask: "Who lost the keys?" (subject -- my roommate). "What did he do?" (verb -- lost). "What did he lose?" (object -- his keys). 2 min.
- Explain: today we practice finding subjects, verbs, and objects so we can write better sentences. 1 min.

stages.stage: Controlled Practice — Practice 3: Subjects, Verbs, and Objects
stages.stage_aim: To give learners structured practice identifying subjects, verbs, and objects using a consistent annotation system
stages.procedure:
- Ss open books to Practice 3 (p. 14). Display instructions on screen: underline S with one line, V with two lines, circle O. Work individually. 5 min.
- Demo item 1 together. Remind Ss: linking verbs (be, become, look, feel, seem, smell, sound, taste) do NOT have objects.
- Pair check. 3 min.
- Whole-class feedback: display answers on screen. Address any disagreements, especially items with linking verbs (1, 5, 6). Discuss items 7, 9 (no object). 4 min.

stages.stage: Semi-Controlled Practice — Practice 4: Editing for Subjects and Verbs
stages.stage_aim: To give learners guided practice identifying and completing sentences that are missing subjects or verbs
stages.procedure:
- Ss turn to Practice 4 -- Larry's Bad Habit (p. 15). Work individually: read the paragraph and add the missing subjects or verbs. 5 min.
- Remind Ss: Look for word groups that feel incomplete. Ask "Who?" or "What action?" to find what's missing.
- Pair check -- compare answers. Some sentences have more than one possible answer. 3 min.
- Display the paragraph on screen. Elicit corrections from different pairs. Discuss alternative answers (e.g., sentence 3: "He" vs "Larry"). 4 min.

stages.stage: Freer Practice — Practice 5: Identifying and Punctuating Sentences
stages.stage_aim: To give learners extended practice applying both sentence-boundary recognition and capitalization rules to an unpunctuated paragraph
stages.procedure:
- Ss turn to Practice 5 -- My Neighbors (p. 15). Work individually: read the paragraph, find where 14 sentences begin and end, add periods and capital letters. 6 min.
- Remind Ss: use the capitalization rules from Part 1 (first word, pronoun I, names, nationalities, places).
- Pair check. 4 min.
- Display the corrected paragraph on screen as a continuous text with capitals in yellow and sentence boundaries marked. Discuss any tricky spots (e.g., "Anju is a wonderful cook" -- already capitalized, no change needed; "a young couple" vs "The husband"). 4 min.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate SVO concepts and connect progress back to the PET writing criteria from Part 1
stages.procedure:
- Quick-fire review: "What does S stand for? V? O?" "What kind of verbs don't have objects?" (linking verbs). 1 min.
- Return to the PET Writing scale: "Now you can write complete sentences, use capitals correctly, AND identify subjects, verbs, and objects. Which Organization and Language bands are you reaching now?" 1 min.
- Preview next topic: "Next time -- describing your classmate!" 1 min.
